profile.name: Chiang Jia Yuan
profile.title: Hardware/Software Integration · From PCB to Firmware to Data
profile.bio: With a mechatronics background, I have worked on circuits, PCB design, embedded firmware, and data analysis. I am studying electrical engineering. After my ICU VAP paper was accepted, I audited its data and evaluation pipeline, found that the original results were affected by the evaluation setup and cohort differences, and reframed the work as a methodology audit. Accepted as a poster at IEEE GCCE 2026.

experience.organization: Yuan Ze Univ. — Prof. Lin Shu-Yan's Lab
experience.description: I worked on an ICU VAP prediction study, handling data preparation, model comparisons, and evaluation. After the paper was accepted, I audited the data indexing, time alignment, and patient-level split, and found that the original high scores were affected by the evaluation setup and cohort-source differences. I reframed the work as a methodology audit. Accepted as a poster at IEEE GCCE 2026.

Engineering Advisor since 2023.
Previously:
Owned robot systems architecture — multi-sensor fusion, PID closed-loop motor control tuning, and hardware/software interface definition; shifted to an operational advisory role as that system was retired.
Now:
Introduced LLM-assisted tools that cut the trial-and-error firmware debugging cycle by about a week, and coach newer members to debug from root cause instead of line-by-line guessing. Also rebuilt the team website to cut repetitive PR inquiries.

The team's utility player — the bridge between mechanical, software, electrical, and PR. Competed in 2 FRC international regional events over 3 years (2020 CSIA 5G Regional and 2022 Taiwan Foxconn Regional), and took part in the National Skills Competition (Team Project category) and the National Vocational High School Craft Competition (Digital Electronics).

projects.title: ICU VAP Prediction: Pilot Methodology Validation
projects.description: A single-center ICU study at Far Eastern Memorial Hospital with 107 patients. After acceptance, I reviewed indexing, time alignment, and evaluation splits and found that window-level splitting and differences in patient sources could inflate results. The current data do not support a clinical performance claim. Accepted as an IEEE GCCE 2026 poster.

images.caption: Pipeline: feature selection → sliding window → LSTM → multi-horizon evaluation
Original window-level baseline comparison; patients crossed the train/test split, so these are not performance claims
Original window-level result plot; the audited setup does not establish patient-level generalization

detail.purpose: The study began by asking whether ICU time series could predict VAP. A post-submission audit found issues in data processing and evaluation, so I examined how those conditions affected the results.
detail.concept: I checked patient, time-window, and label alignment, and whether the same patient appeared in both training and test data. Ventilator brand and enrollment year were also associated with labels, so source effects cannot be ruled out.
detail.outcome: The study currently supports conclusions about evaluation limits: window-level splitting can inflate scores, and source differences may provide shortcuts. Assessing clinical signals will require consistent sources and clear time definitions. Accepted as an IEEE GCCE 2026 poster.

items.name: LSTM Time-Series Modeling
items.desc: Built a three-layer TensorFlow/Keras LSTM classifier and compared window lengths and smaller models. Results on this small single-center cohort require patient-level splitting and source-stratified interpretation.

items.name: Class Imbalance Handling
items.desc: Applied SMOTE within each training fold to keep synthetic samples out of test folds. Later experiments did not establish that GAN or other augmentation methods outperform no augmentation or SMOTE.

items.name: Explainable AI (XAI)
items.desc: Integrated Gradients was used to inspect feature contributions. Feature selection and attribution rankings were affected by full-dataset selection and data-processing issues, so the Top 4 ranking is not treated as stable.

items.name: Leakage-Free Validation
items.desc: Used patient-level splits to check whether one patient crossed the training and test sets. The MIMIC-IV replication and FEMH analysis are separate experiments; neither is used here to claim clinical prediction performance.

items.name: Per-fold Normalization
items.desc: Computed normalization statistics independently inside each cross-validation fold to keep test-fold statistics out of training.

items.name: Ablation Study
items.desc: Removing mv_total (mv≡Vt×RR) improved AUROC and AUPRC under the window-level setup. This analysis was not rerun with the corrected patient-level evaluation and is not a current conclusion.

items.name: Sliding Window Construction
items.desc: Converted ICU time series into fixed-length windows for each prediction horizon. Splits must group by patient so windows from one patient cannot cross folds.

items.name: Physiological Signal Preprocessing
items.desc: Used pandas and NumPy to prepare multi-source vital-sign and ventilator data. The audit corrected time-alignment and field-overwrite issues, showing why each source needs explicit checks.

projects.title: AWS × BitoPro Hackathon: BitOGuard
projects.description: Our three-person team reached the AWS × BitoPro Hackathon final and completed the event without placing. The system combines LightGBM and XGBoost, analyzes transaction accounts, uses 32 behavioral features, and applies SHAP to inspect model predictions.

images.caption: Dashboard overview: AUC 83.2%, Precision 27.5%, Recall 33.2%, confusion matrix + 5-fold CV bar chart
Account risk query: USER ID 971465 scored 82.1% — classified as extreme high risk, blacklisted
Risk ranking: Top 50 high-risk (CRITICAL) vs. Top 50 low-risk accounts
Model evaluation: feature importance (total_volume highest) + decision threshold analysis (optimal 0.24)
Predictions: 12,753 users — 501 flagged as risk (3.93%), 12,252 normal (96.07%)

detail.purpose: The challenge was to identify potentially fraudulent accounts from transaction data. I worked on the model, data processing, and parts of the cloud workflow; the team presented risk scores in a review dashboard.
detail.concept: The model blends LightGBM and XGBoost at 0.6/0.4 and uses 32 behavioral features. The project also includes S3, Glue, Athena, SageMaker, Lambda, and Streamlit components. SHAP shows feature contributions to predictions.
detail.outcome: The team reached the final and completed the event, without a placement. Five-fold OOF AUROC was 0.832, with 27.5% precision and 33.2% recall. These are competition dataset results, not evidence of deployment in a financial institution.

items.name: Gradient Boosting Classification
items.desc: LightGBM for imbalanced binary classification; tune max_depth, learning_rate, num_iterations, and class weighting, then compare precision and recall across decision thresholds

items.name: Behavioral Feature Engineering
items.desc: Extracting 32 behavioral indicators from TWD and USDT transaction records (frequency, late-night ratio, blacklist neighbor count, etc.), verifying actual model gains from expanding the initial 3-feature set

items.name: SHAP Interpretability
items.desc: Computing each feature's marginal contribution per account; distinguishing global feature importance from per-account local explanations to support AML compliance reporting

items.name: End-to-End Data Pipeline
items.desc: Designed S3→Glue ETL→Athena→SageMaker→Lambda 6-service chain; mastering data format transformation, error propagation, and permission design between nodes; CloudFormation IaC for reproducibility

items.name: Graph-Based Multi-hop Analysis
items.desc: Glue + Athena SQL for second-degree blacklist neighbor query; understanding the approximate computation of graph-theory features in relational databases and query complexity

items.name: Event-Driven Inference
items.desc: Lambda receives trigger events and calls SageMaker endpoints for real-time prediction; understanding cold-start latency and sync/async tradeoffs for AML real-time detection

projects.title: Analog Circuit Implementation: Audio Amplifier PCB Design
projects.description: A two-stage BJT audio amplifier for a sophomore electronics lab. My teammate handled the breadboard and PSpice; I prepared the schematic, routed the PCB, etched and soldered the board, and debugged it. Two rebuilds fixed a copper short and mirrored component footprints; an 8Ω speaker played audio.

images.caption: Final product: two-stage BJT amplifier board + 8Ω speaker, driving audio output
Photoresist-etched PCB blank: clear traces, ready for drilling and soldering
EDA schematic: CE amplifier stage + bias network + CC emitter follower
PCB component placement (top): 109.2×45.7mm, transistors, capacitors, trimpots
PCB component placement (bottom): confirming mirrored pin orientation — key lesson from two rebuilds
PCB copper traces: full routing for CE + CC stages
PCB drill pattern: all component pads and mounting hole machining reference

detail.purpose: The lab required a two-stage BJT audio amplifier. I translated the circuit into a PCB and made and debugged the physical board.
detail.concept: My work covered schematic cleanup, PCB routing, photoresist etching, soldering, and power-on checks. The first rebuild fixed a short from residual copper; the second corrected component footprint orientation.
detail.outcome: The finished circuit played through an 8Ω speaker. I worked through the full path from schematic and PCB layout to hardware debugging.

items.name: CE Amplifier Bias Design
items.desc: Calculating R3/R4 voltage divider bias to stabilize Q1 in active region; understanding the tradeoffs between β, DC operating point, and thermal stability in component selection

items.name: CC Emitter Follower
items.desc: Emitter resistor RE introduces negative feedback for low output impedance, reducing loading effects between stages; voltage gain approaches 1

items.name: Bias Stabilization Design
items.desc: D1–D4 in series provide stable voltage difference to Q2/Q3 bases; C3 absorbs turn-off transient reverse voltage; understanding how diode forward voltage temperature characteristics affect bias stability

items.name: Variable Gain Adjustment
items.desc: Rv1a/Rv1b control input signal strength; Rv2 fine-tunes DC operating point; experimentally finding the maximum linear gain boundary without distortion

items.name: Layout Routing Design
items.desc: Hand-drawn double-sided PCB; routing under components to reduce white-line crossings; completed full exposure→development→acid etching process

items.name: Systematic Circuit Debugging
items.desc: Two rebuilds established a debugging flow from component-by-component verification (continuity, saturation, charge) to board-layer short detection; identified residual-copper shorts and pin mirror errors as root causes

items.name: Simulation vs. Real-World Comparison
items.desc: SPICE simulation of time-domain waveform and Bode plot frequency response, then oscilloscope measurement of actual output; analyzing deviations caused by non-ideal component characteristics

projects.title: PCB Trace Defect Detection: Tiled Object Detection with Azure Custom Vision
projects.description: Uses Azure Custom Vision to detect missing holes, mouse bites, and open circuits in PCB images. Training images are split into 600px tiles; inference scans overlapping windows and merges boxes with NMS. A Flask tool supports batch inspection and feedback. The README reports 82% mAP and 100% precision.

images.caption: Custom Vision training summary: the public README reports 100% precision and 82% mAP
Inspection tool & human-feedback retrain loop: upload → tiled detect → batch stats → manual correction → review/approve → retrain on approved data only
Training data: each board is sliced into 600px tiles centered on defects, raising defect-to-tile ratio from ~2% to ~12% (green = ground truth)
Held-out boards 09–12 (zoomed): green = ground truth, red = model prediction, across all three defect classes
Full-board detection: tiled inference on a held-out board (type 09) with boxes mapped back to the original image
missing_hole detection — board 09, #1 (green = ground truth, red = prediction)
missing_hole detection — board 11, #1 (green = ground truth, red = prediction)
mouse_bite detection — board 09, #1 (green = ground truth, red = prediction)
mouse_bite detection — board 11, #1 (green = ground truth, red = prediction)
open_circuit detection — board 09, #1 (green = ground truth, red = prediction)
open_circuit detection — board 11, #1 (green = ground truth, red = prediction)

detail.purpose: Full-board images were too large to pass directly to the object detector. I tiled the training images and built an inference flow that scans the board and merges duplicate detections.
detail.concept: The training process creates 600px tiles. Inference uses overlapping windows, then NMS to consolidate detections. A Flask tool supports batch checks and human feedback. README metrics are project evaluation results, not a guarantee across all board types.
detail.outcome: The project README reports 82% mAP and 100% precision and shows validation on held-out board types. The workflow covers tiling, whole-board scanning, result consolidation, and feedback.

items.name: Image Tiling
items.desc: Slice 600px tiles centered on each defect box, keep a box only if ≥40% of its area is inside the tile, re-normalize to 0–1; defect ratio rises from ~2% to ~12%, the make-or-break step of the project

items.name: Pascal VOC Parsing
items.desc: Parse bndbox with xml.etree.ElementTree and convert pixel coordinates to the 0–1 normalized form Custom Vision requires

items.name: Azure Custom Vision SDK
items.desc: Full flow via the Python SDK: create project (compact domain), batch-upload images with regions, Advanced Training, publish, export TensorFlow; Advanced was chosen over Quick Train on purpose

items.name: model.pb Export and Colab Loading
items.desc: Export the frozen graph model.pb (input Placeholder:0, output model_outputs:0), load it in Colab with tf.compat.v1; the YOLO-style anchor/NMS decoding reuses the official object_detection.py

items.name: Tiled Inference + NMS
items.desc: Detect a full board tile by tile, map predictions back to the original image, then drop duplicate boxes from overlapping tiles with NMS at IoU 0.3

items.name: Held-out Validation
items.desc: Generalization test on 106 images from board types 09–12 that never appeared in training, drawing green (ground truth) and red (prediction) boxes; 538 ground-truth defects against 509 predicted boxes, validating performance on new boards rather than trusting the cross-validation numbers alone

items.name: Batch inspection UI
items.desc: Local Flask web app: drag many boards for batch detection, draw the three defect classes in distinct colors, summarize NG/OK and per-class counts, export CSV

items.name: Human-feedback loop
items.desc: Detections can be marked as false positive or missed and saved as corrections; after human review/approval, only approved data is used to retrain — an active-learning loop

projects.title: Wireless Whack-a-Mole (Special Ed Aid)
projects.description: Built a wireless whack-a-mole teaching aid for the Nangang VHS special education department. ESP32/ESP-NOW connects one master to four game units. I fixed component damage caused by relay-coil back-EMF, then addressed 7805 overheating. The department issued a letter of appreciation.

detail.purpose: The special education department needed an interactive teaching aid that was easy to operate and maintain. We chose a whack-a-mole format with one master controlling four wireless units.
detail.concept: ESP32 boards send game states over ESP-NOW; buttons and relays control each unit. I added a 1N4001 flyback diode across relay coils to handle back-EMF, then checked the load and heat dissipation around the 7805 linear regulator.
detail.outcome: Five units were assembled and delivered to the department, which issued a letter of appreciation. I worked through wireless communication, relay protection, and linear-regulator heating.

items.name: Multi-Unit P2P Coordination
items.desc: Designed 1-master 4-slave broadcast state machine; mastered ESP-NOW device pairing, broadcast reset, and auto-reconnect in a router-free environment; implemented master/slave logic in Arduino C++

items.name: Transistor Current Amplification
items.desc: Calculated 9013 NPN base current-limiting resistor for saturation conduction, solving ESP32 GPIO current insufficient to directly drive relay

items.name: High-Voltage Load Isolation
items.desc: Relay fully isolates 3.3V control from 11.1V load; understanding contact capacity limits and switching frequency effects on contact lifespan

items.name: Back-EMF Protection
items.desc: 1N4001 flyback diode across relay coil absorbs inductive back-EMF on turn-off; necessity understood only after diagnosing actual ESP32 failure in the field

items.name: Power Regulation & Decoupling
items.desc: 7805 linear regulator with ceramic decoupling capacitors to eliminate power glitches from motor/relay switching; diagnosed 7805 overheating and understood linear regulator power dissipation limits

items.name: Quick-Swap Structure
items.desc: "Keep it simple" principle: top cover changed from 3D print to wood to shorten replacement time; magnetic bottom cover for tool-free battery access, designed specifically for on-site special education maintenance needs

projects.title: Team-Built Competition Robot
projects.description: Represented Nangang VHS at the 2022 52nd National Skills Competition in the Team Project category. Three students built a gripper robot. I handled 24V power distribution, the relay H-bridge, and vehicle wiring; teammates handled mechanical fabrication and control software.

detail.purpose: The competition asked a three-person team to build a robot that could move and grip objects within a limited time. I handled the electrical system and integrated it with the mechanical and software work.
detail.concept: I designed the relay H-bridge, planned 24V power distribution, and wired the robot. Teammates fabricated the chassis and gripper and wrote the control software.
detail.outcome: We completed the school project for the 52nd National Skills Competition. The work required integrating electrical, mechanical, and control systems under a short deadline.

items.name: Relay H-Bridge Drive
items.desc: Two relays per axis form a single-axis H-bridge to switch motor current direction; understanding H-bridge same-side relay simultaneous conduction short-circuit risk and interlock design

items.name: 24V High-Voltage Wiring
items.desc: Lead-acid battery pack high-current wiring standards; understanding the effect of wire cross-section and connector contact resistance on power loss

items.name: Universal Gripper Design
items.desc: Curved gripping surface for cylinders, flat surface for rectangular objects — accommodating two cross-sections without tool changes; understanding geometric constraints for gripping stability

projects.title: Swerve Drive Omnidirectional Research
projects.description: Worked across three iterations of an FRC swerve-drive chassis, including LabVIEW kinematics, gear transmission, CAD, CNC milling, and wire EDM. The 2022 robot received the Innovation in Control Award at the FRC Taiwan Fuhong Regional.

detail.purpose: The team iterated on its swerve-drive chassis, changing motion control, transmission, and fabrication between versions. I contributed to the control code, gear design, and part production.
detail.concept: I implemented omnidirectional kinematics in LabVIEW and worked on gear transmission, CAD, CNC milling, and wire EDM. The chassis versions represent design and fabrication work across multiple team members.
detail.outcome: The 2022 chassis competed at the FRC Taiwan Fuhong Regional and received the Innovation in Control Award. An earlier robot competed at the 2020 FRC Central Taiwan 5G Regional and received the Excellence in Engineering Award.

items.name: Vector-Composition Kinematics
items.desc: Decomposing translation, rotation, and arc motion modes as X∠θ vectors and superimposing them; normalizing by max-force wheel to prevent motor saturation; fully implemented in LabVIEW graphical programming

items.name: PID Closed-Loop Control
items.desc: Per-wheel independent encoder feedback for PID steering angle control; mastering integral windup and derivative filtering tuning in high-dynamic competition environments

items.name: Modular Transmission Architecture
items.desc: Drive and steering motor holes shared; gear zone swappable for reduction ratio adjustment without modifying aluminum plates; three-generation iteration validated modular design's improvement in repair speed

items.name: Lightweight Structural Design
items.desc: Material substitution for weight reduction: internal gears switched to FDM printing, retaining metal motor shaft gears; CNC material removal from aluminum plates while maintaining structural strength

items.name: CNC Numerical Milling
items.desc: Machining transmission shafts (hex & square cross-sections) with 4-jaw chuck positioning; bilateral milling for cross-sectional symmetry; significantly improved dimensional accuracy and batch reproducibility over manual milling

items.name: Wire EDM
items.desc: M1.25–M1.5 spur and bevel gear profile and bore cutting; mastering clamp plate fixturing, edge-finding XY error correction, and path simulation verification workflow
